title: Playing the Heavy Wing
youtubeTitle: Subspace Lattice Academy Ep.8 — Refractors, Carriers & the Anomaly Slice
description: Optional Advanced modules: Refractor Wing and Fleet Draft. Net law for diagonals and omni-slides, Hub-anchor tether, material hierarchy, and the Anomaly Slice blind spot. Companion to docs/advanced-manual.pdf Part I.

scenes.headline: Playing the Heavy Wing
scenes.subhead: Refractors, Carriers, and why orthogonal walls are incomplete safety.
scenes.voiceover: Episode eight: the Heavy wing. Rated play opens with twin Beams. Lobby Advanced modules can authorize Refractor Wing or Fleet Draft — same Sensor Net law, wider geometry.

scenes.headline: Two lobby packages
bullets: Refractor Wing — Beam + Refractor on files 3 and 7
Fleet Draft — Refractor + Hub-anchored Carrier on those files
Infiltrators shift outward so the wing does not stack
scenes.voiceover: In the lobby, Advanced modules offer Refractor Wing — a Beam paired with a Refractor on files three and seven — or Fleet Draft, which swaps in a Hub-anchored Carrier beside the Refractor. Infiltrators shift to keep the opening legal. Learn both as one system with Standard Beams.

scenes.headline: Heavy profiles: The Beam
bullets: Beam — orthogonal slide inside your Sensor Net

scenes.headline: Heavy profiles: The Refractor
bullets: Refractor — diagonal slide, same net constraint
scenes.voiceover: Refractors cut diagonal vectors across Chebyshev radiation — including seams that brush the Anomalous Core’s corners.

scenes.headline: Heavy profiles: The Carrier
bullets: Carrier — omni slide while Hub-tethered; crawl when drifting
scenes.voiceover: Carriers are fortress queens while tethered to the Hub within radius three under fleet defaults; drift outside that tether and the Carrier crawls one step. Target Lock still reduces any of them to a single orthogonal crawl.

Missions one through three stay on Standard Beams so the rated opening stays readable. When you flip on a Heavy wing, the back-rank corners change — heavies park on files three and seven, already inside the opening net — but Hub safety and refuse-the-hang do not change.

scenes.headline: Opening with the wing
bullets: Park heavies on 3 and 7 inside the opening glow
Diagonals matter from ply one under Refractor Wing
Fleet Draft: treat the Carrier as a home-rank fortress
Early Carrier aggression that snaps the tether buys a crawl
scenes.voiceover: Openings with the wing: park heavies on three and seven while they still sit in the starting Sensor Net. A Refractor contests the center differently than a Beam — diagonals matter immediately. Under Fleet Draft, keep the Carrier as a home-rank fortress. Pushing it up the board early trades capital mobility for a crawl when the Hub-anchor snaps.

scenes.headline: Heavy-piece hierarchy
bullets: Refractor — high coverage, specialized material
Beam ↔ Refractor trades are usually lateral
Escort for Refractor is a massive tactical win
Carrier — maximum material, conditional tempo
scenes.voiceover: Price the wing correctly. A Refractor commands diagonal reach but cannot hold a pure orthogonal file. Trading Beam for Refractor is usually lateral; taking a Refractor with an Escort is a huge win. A tethered Carrier dominates material and coverage; an untethered one is a foot soldier until it re-enters Hub radiation.

Midgame Standard Beams pressure. Orthogonal screens and Beam ranks feel safe — especially with the Gravity Well blocking through-traffic on its row and file. That comfort is exactly where the Refractor lesson lives.

scenes.headline: The Anomaly Slice — the 45-ply blind spot
bullets: Setup: White’s Beams screen the Hub on ranks and files
Execution: Black’s Refractor rides a diagonal past a (5,5) corner
Lesson: orthogonal safety is incomplete safety
scenes.voiceover: Pedagogical highlight from the advanced manual. Setup: White builds a strong orthogonal blockade with Beams, screening the Hub. Execution: Black maneuvers a Refractor into active Sensor Net on a diagonal that brushes a corner of the Anomaly at five-five. Lesson: the diagonal slide bypasses the Beam wall and can force a Target Lock — or open a Surgical Strike lane the screen never saw.

scenes.headline: Add two questions to the look-ahead
bullets: Are my corners open to a Refractor slice?
Is their Carrier tethered or drifting?
Scan Beam files and Refractor diagonals for Hub mates
Refuse hangs on both geometries
scenes.voiceover: When the wing is live, extend the look-ahead. Can you take their Hub on a Beam file or a Refractor diagonal? Can they take yours after your move — including diagonal answers. Are your corners exposed to an Anomaly slice? Is the enemy Carrier within Hub radius three, or already drifting into a crawl?

Contested Space and Target Lock still rule the midgame. A locked Refractor is a wall ornament. A locked Carrier loses its slide and is reduced to a single orthogonal crawl. Do not overextend a heavy into enemy glow just because it looks expensive — locked value is zero mobility.

scenes.headline: Win conditions do not change
bullets: Surgical Strike — Hub capture
Sector Integration — coverage clock after activation
Heavies change which geometries feed those wins
Not a third victory type
scenes.voiceover: Expanded branching from Refractors and Carriers does not add a new win condition. You still end by Surgical Strike or by Sector Integration after the clock arms. The wing only changes which lanes and diagonals feed those finishes — and which blind spots punish captains who only scan files.

scenes.headline: Authorize the wing — keep the scan
scenes.nextEpisode: Practice Refractor Wing & Fleet Draft vs AI · Advanced manual Part I
scenes.voiceover: That is the Heavy wing: same net law, diagonal and omni geometry, Carrier tether discipline, and the Anomaly Slice. Open the advanced manual’s Part I, flip on a lobby module, and keep refusing the hang — on files and on diagonals.
